prompts.title: Nightly Memory Consolidation
prompts.description: Set up an always-on automation that runs every night at 3 AM to consolidate daily memory files into long-term storage. Finds all daily memory files from the past 24 hours, merges unique entries into your main long-term memory file, deduplicates by content match, and logs the results. Alerts you via Telegram when complete.
prompts.prompt_text:
Set up an always-on automation that runs every night at 3 AM to consolidate daily memory files into long-term storage.

OBJECTIVE: Find all daily memory files created in the past 24 hours, read their contents, merge unique entries into the main long-term memory file, deduplicate by exact content match, and log the results.

DIRECTORIES:
- Daily memories: memory/daily/*.md
- Main long-term memory: memory/longterm.md
- Log file: memory/consolidation.log

PROCESS:
1. List all files in memory/daily/ modified in the last 24 hours using exec with 'find memory/daily/ -type f -mtime -1'
2. Read each daily file using filesystem
3. Load existing longterm.md
4. For each entry in daily files, check if it already exists in longterm.md (by exact content match)
5. Append only new unique entries to longterm.md
6. Archive processed daily files to memory/archive/YYYY-MM-DD.bak
7. Write consolidation summary to memory/consolidation.log

OUTPUT: A consolidation report: timestamp, files processed, entries examined, new entries added, duplicates skipped, any errors.

TOOLS: exec, cron, filesystem

ALERT: After each run, send a brief Telegram message: 'Memory consolidation complete: X new entries merged, Y duplicates skipped.'
setup_steps: Create directories: memory/daily, memory/archive, memory/
Create longterm.md with header: "# Long-term Memory" if it doesn't exist
Create an empty consolidation.log file
Add to crontab: "0 3 * * *" pointing to the consolidation script
Test by running with sample daily files first
Verify log rotation for consolidation.log

Entries: 34 examined
Added: 12 new
Skipped: 22 duplicates

prompts.title: Heartbeat Monitor
prompts.description: Set up an always-on automation that pings a configurable list of service URLs every 5 minutes and immediately alerts you via Telegram when any service goes down. Logs all results with timestamps. Handles timeouts, DNS failures, and SSL errors as failures.
prompts.prompt_text:
Set up an always-on automation that pings a configurable list of service URLs every 5 minutes and alerts you immediately when any service goes down.

CONFIGURATION:
- services.txt: one URL per line (e.g., https://api.yoursite.com/health)
- log file: ~/logs/heartbeat.log

PROCESS:
1. Read all URLs from services.txt
2. For each URL, run: curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -L --max-time 10 [URL]
3. Log each result with timestamp to heartbeat.log: '[TIME] | [URL] | [STATUS] | [RESPONSE_MS]ms'
4. If status != 200, immediately send Telegram alert via message tool

ALERT FORMAT:
"🚨 Service Down: [URL] returned [STATUS] at [TIME]
Response time: [X]ms"

TOOLS: exec, cron, filesystem, message

The script must handle connection timeouts (status 000), DNS failures, and SSL errors as failures.
setup_steps: Create services.txt with one URL per line
Create script: ~/scripts/heartbeat.sh that loops through services.txt
Make script executable: chmod +x ~/scripts/heartbeat.sh
Add to crontab: "*/5 * * * *" ~/scripts/heartbeat.sh
Test manually: run script and verify log output
Verify Telegram bot is configured in OpenClaw message tool

prompts.title: Disk Space Alert System
prompts.description: Set up an always-on automation that checks disk usage on all mounted volumes every 10 minutes and alerts you via Telegram when any volume exceeds 85% capacity. Logs all readings. Critical alerts at 90%.
prompts.prompt_text:
Set up an always-on automation that checks disk usage on all mounted volumes every 10 minutes and alerts you via Telegram when any volume exceeds 85% capacity.

PROCESS:
1. Run: df -h (excluding tmpfs/snap/virtual filesystems)
2. Parse output to extract: filesystem, total size, used space, usage percentage
3. For each volume, check if usage % > 85
4. Log all readings to ~/logs/disk_usage.log with timestamp
5. If any volume > 85%, immediately send Telegram alert

ALERT FORMAT:
"💾 Disk Alert: [VOLUME] at [USAGE]%
Total: [SIZE] | Used: [USED] | Available: [AVAIL]
Time: [TIMESTAMP]"

For volumes > 90%: escalate with '🔴 CRITICAL' prefix.

TOOLS: exec, cron, filesystem, message
setup_steps: Create log directory: mkdir -p ~/logs
Create script: ~/scripts/disk_check.sh that runs df -h and parses output
Make executable: chmod +x ~/scripts/disk_check.sh
Add to crontab: "*/10 * * * *" ~/scripts/disk_check.sh
Test manually: run script and check log file output
Verify Telegram bot is working before enabling alert mode

prompts.title: Session Health Monitor
prompts.description: Set up an always-on automation that checks the health of all OpenClaw sessions every 15 minutes, identifies stale or unresponsive sessions, recovers or archives them, and sends you a Telegram digest of what was found.
prompts.prompt_text:
Set up an always-on automation that checks the health of all OpenClaw sessions every 15 minutes, identifies stale or unresponsive sessions, and either recovers or archives them.

PROCESS:
1. Use sessions_list to retrieve all active sessions with their last activity timestamps
2. For each session, determine if last activity > 30 minutes ago
3. For sessions inactive > 30 min: use sessions_send with a lightweight echo to test responsiveness
4. If no response within 10 seconds: mark as stale
5. For stale sessions: log to ~/logs/stale_sessions.log
6. Archive stale sessions using exec to remove their session files from ~/.openclaw/sessions/
7. Send a summary digest to Telegram

THRESHOLD: 30 minutes of inactivity = stale

TOOLS: sessions_list, sessions_send, exec, filesystem, message, cron
setup_steps: Verify sessions_list returns all expected sessions
Create ~/logs/ directory for session logs
Create script: ~/scripts/session_health.sh following the PROCESS above
Make executable: chmod +x ~/scripts/session_health.sh
Add to crontab: "*/15 * * * *" ~/scripts/session_health.sh
Test manually with --dry-run first to verify correct session paths
Set up Telegram bot for alert delivery

prompts.title: Automated Git Commit Watcher
prompts.description: Set up an always-on automation that watches a specific directory for file changes every 10 minutes and automatically commits any uncommitted changes to git with a timestamped commit message listing exactly which files changed. Never auto-commits to main.
prompts.prompt_text:
Set up an always-on automation that watches a specific directory (e.g., ~/projects/myapp) for file changes every 10 minutes, and automatically commits any uncommitted changes to git with a timestamped commit message listing exactly which files changed.

PROCESS:
1. Run: cd ~/projects/myapp && git status --porcelain to get list of changed files
2. If no changes: exit silently
3. If changes exist:
   a. git add -A
   b. git commit -m '[AUTOMATED] Updates $(date +%Y-%m-%d_%H:%M): Changed files: [file1], [file2], ...'
   c. git push origin [current-branch]
4. Log commit details to ~/logs/git_auto_commit.log
5. Send Telegram confirmation with file list

EXCLUDE PATTERNS:
- node_modules/
- .git/
- *.log
- .env
- build/dist/ directories

BRANCH HANDLING: Only commit to development or feature branches. Never auto-commit to main/master.

TOOLS: exec, cron, filesystem, message
setup_steps: Navigate to ~/projects/myapp and verify git repo is initialized
Create .gitignore with EXCLUDE PATTERNS above
Create script: ~/scripts/git_watcher.sh following the PROCESS above
Make executable: chmod +x ~/scripts/git_watcher.sh
Add to crontab: "*/10 * * * *" ~/scripts/git_watcher.sh
Test manually: make a change, run script, verify commit appears in git log
Verify Telegram bot is configured for commit notifications

prompts.title: Nightly Backup Automation
prompts.description: Set up an always-on automation that runs every night at 2 AM, creates a compressed timestamped backup of your critical directories (workspace, memory, config, scripts), stores it locally, verifies with checksum, and sends you a confirmation via Telegram. Auto-deletes backups older than 30 days.
prompts.prompt_text:
Set up an always-on automation that runs every night at 2 AM, creates a compressed timestamped backup of your critical directories, stores it locally with a dated filename, and sends you a confirmation when complete.

DIRECTORIES TO BACKUP:
- ~/.openclaw/workspace/
- ~/.openclaw/memory/
- ~/.openclaw/config/
- ~/scripts/

PROCESS:
1. Create backup directory: ~/backups/
2. Create filename: backup_YYYY-MM-DD.tar.gz
3. Run: tar -czf ~/backups/backup_YYYY-MM-DD.tar.gz [directories above]
4. Verify backup with: tar -tzf filename.tar.gz | wc -l (confirm file count)
5. Calculate checksum: shasum -a 256 filename.tar.gz
6. Log backup details to ~/logs/backups.log
7. Send Telegram confirmation with backup size, file count, and checksum

RETENTION: Delete backups older than 30 days automatically.

TOOLS: exec, cron, filesystem, message
setup_steps: Create ~/backups/ directory
Create ~/logs/ directory if not exists
Create script: ~/scripts/nightly_backup.sh following the PROCESS above
Make executable: chmod +x ~/scripts/nightly_backup.sh
Test manually: run script, verify backup file in ~/backups/
Add to crontab: "0 2 * * *" ~/scripts/nightly_backup.sh
Verify Telegram notifications are working

prompts.title: OpenClaw Access Counter
prompts.description: Set up an always-on automation that tracks how often each of your memory files is accessed. Every read gets logged. Runs a daily analysis that identifies your most-accessed and never-accessed files, so you know what to promote to long-term memory and what to archive. Results sent to Telegram.
prompts.prompt_text:
Set up an always-on automation that tracks how often each of your memory files is accessed. Every time a memory file is read, append an entry to an access log. Run a daily analysis that identifies your most-accessed and never-accessed files, so you can decide what to promote to long-term memory and what to archive.

LOG FORMAT (access_log.jsonl):
{"timestamp": "ISO8601", "file": "memory/path/to/file.md", "action": "read", "access_count": 1}

PROCESS:
1. Create access_log.jsonl in memory/ directory
2. Create a tracking wrapper script that: reads target memory file, increments access count for that file in access_log.jsonl, returns content
3. For each read operation on memory files, use the wrapper instead of direct filesystem reads
4. Daily at midnight: run analysis on access_log.jsonl
5. Generate report: files accessed >10 times this week (hot), files accessed 0 times in 30 days (cold)
6. Send report to Telegram

ANALYSIS:
- Hot files (>10 accesses): promote to long-term memory
- Cold files (0 accesses in 30 days): consider archiving

TOOLS: exec, filesystem, cron, message
setup_steps: Create memory/access_log.jsonl with header: {"access_log": []}
Create tracking script: ~/scripts/memory_tracker.sh
Update relevant memory read operations to use the tracker wrapper
Create analysis script: ~/scripts/memory_stats.sh for midnight analysis
Add to crontab: "0 0 * * *" for daily analysis
Test by manually triggering analysis and checking output
Verify Telegram bot receives the daily report

prompts.title: Keyword Sentiment Tracker
prompts.description: Monitors Reddit, Twitter/X, and web mentions of any keyword you specify, analyzes sentiment across sources, and sends a daily summary to Telegram with volume trends and top discussions.
prompts.prompt_text:
Set up an always-on automation that monitors mentions of a keyword across Reddit, Twitter/X, and the web — then sends you a daily sentiment digest on Telegram.

CONFIGURATION:
Create a config file at ~/configs/sentiment_config.json:
{
  "keyword": "YOUR_KEYWORD",
  "subreddits": ["relevant1", "relevant2"],
  "twitter_handles": ["handle1", "handle2"],
  "telegram_chat_id": "YOUR_CHAT_ID"
}

PROCESS:
1. REDDIT SEARCH: Use web_search to query "site:reddit.com KEYWORD" and also "KEYWORD reddit" — retrieve top 5 results from the last 7 days
2. TWITTER/X SEARCH: Use web_search to query "KEYWORD site:x.com OR site:twitter.com since:2026-01-01" — retrieve top 10 tweets/reposts
3. GENERAL WEB: Use web_search to query "KEYWORD" (no site filter) — get top 5 articles from the last 7 days
4. For each source, read the page/content using web_fetch to extract:
   - Reddit: post title, score, number of comments, subreddit, flaired sentiment if visible
   - Twitter: tweet text, likes, retweets, reply count
   - Web: article headline, publication, key pull quotes

SENTIMENT ANALYSIS (manual classification):
Classify each mention as POSITIVE, NEGATIVE, or NEUTRAL based on:
- POSITIVE: praise, excitement, recommendations, problem solved, ROI, growth
- NEGATIVE: complaints, bugs, outages, failures, regrets, cancellations, scams
- NEUTRAL: news articles, announcements, how-to guides, comparisons without opinion

Score: POSITIVE = +1, NEGATIVE = -1, NEUTRAL = 0
Sentiment Score = sum(scores) / total_mentions (range -1 to +1)

DAILY DIGEST FORMAT (send via message tool to Telegram):
📊 *Keyword Sentiment Report — [DATE]*

🔍 *Volume:* X mentions today (vs Y yesterday)
😊/😐/😠 *Sentiment:* X% positive / X% neutral / X% negative
📈 *Score:* X.XX (range -1 to +1)

*Top Positive Mentions:*
• [Source] — [1-2 sentence summary]

*Top Negative Mentions:*
• [Source] — [1-2 sentence summary]

*Key Discussions:*
• [Source] — [1-sentence takeaway]

TOOLS: web_search, web_fetch, exec, cron, message
setup_steps: Create ~/configs/ directory and sentiment_config.json with your keyword, target subreddits, and Twitter handles
Create a script at ~/scripts/sentiment_tracker.sh that runs the full monitoring pipeline
Make the script executable: chmod +x ~/scripts/sentiment_tracker.sh
Add to crontab: "0 9 * * *" to run every morning at 9 AM (adjust as needed)
Test manually: run the script with a test keyword and verify the Telegram digest looks correct
Verify your Telegram bot can send to the configured chat ID

prompts.title: Competitor Change Detector
prompts.description: Watches a competitor website or blog and notifies you via Telegram when they publish new content, change pricing, or update key pages — keeping you ahead of market moves.
prompts.prompt_text:
Set up an always-on automation that watches a competitor website or blog and notifies you via Telegram when they publish new content or change pricing.

CONFIGURATION:
Create ~/configs/competitor_config.json:
{
  "competitors": [
    {
      "name": "CompetitorName",
      "blog_url": "https://competitor.com/blog",
      "pricing_url": "https://competitor.com/pricing",
      "sitemap_url": "https://competitor.com/sitemap.xml"
    }
  ],
  "check_interval_hours": 6,
  "state_file": "~/.openclaw/competitor_state.json"
}

STATE FILE:
Track last known state to detect changes:
{
  "competitor.com/blog": {
    "last_urls": ["article-1", "article-2"],
    "last_check": 1744156800,
    "pricing_hash": "sha256_of_pricing_page"
  }
}

PROCESS:
1. Read the competitor sitemap using web_fetch to get all blog post URLs
2. Filter to posts published or updated in the last 7 days
3. Compare against state_file last known URLs
4. NEW CONTENT: For any new posts found:
   a. Fetch the article with web_fetch
   b. Extract: title, publish date, excerpt (first 200 chars), estimated read time
   c. Classify content type: announcement, tutorial, comparison, pricing update, case study
5. PRICING CHANGES: For pricing_url:
   a. Fetch page and compute SHA-256 hash of the raw text
   b. Compare to stored hash in state_file
   c. If changed: fetch the full page and extract what changed (added/removed features, price changes)
6. Update state_file with new URLs and hashes
7. If changes found: send Telegram alert immediately

ALERT FORMAT (message tool to Telegram):
🔍 *Competitor Alert: [CompetitorName]*

📝 *New Content ({count}):*
• [Post Title](URL) — {type} — {excerpt}

{If pricing changed:}
💰 *Pricing Update:*
{Before: bullet of old pricing} → {After: bullet of new pricing}

🕐 *Checked:* [timestamp]

TOOLS: web_fetch, exec, cron, message, filesystem
setup_steps: Create ~/configs/competitor_config.json with your competitor URLs and check interval
Create the state file at ~/.openclaw/competitor_state.json (initially empty dict {})
Create script: ~/scripts/competitor_check.sh that runs the full pipeline
Make executable: chmod +x ~/scripts/competitor_check.sh
Add to crontab: "0 */6 * * *" to check every 6 hours
Test manually first: run with --verbose and check output
Verify Telegram bot is configured

prompts.title: ArXiv Paper Alert
prompts.description: Watches arXiv for new papers matching keywords you care about, sends abstracts to Telegram with link, authors, and relevance score so you never miss a relevant paper.
prompts.prompt_text:
Set up an always-on automation that watches arXiv for new papers matching keywords you care about, sends abstracts to Telegram with link, authors, and relevance score.

CONFIGURATION:
Create ~/configs/arxiv_config.json:
{
  "keywords": ["decentralized finance", "layer 2 scaling", "zero knowledge proofs"],
  "categories": ["cs.CR", "cs.LO", "q-fin.TR"],
  "max_results_per_keyword": 3,
  "state_file": "~/.openclaw/arxiv_state.json"
}

STATE FILE:
Track papers already sent to avoid duplicates:
{
  "sent_ids": ["2301.12345", "2301.12346"],
  "last_check": 1744156800
}

PROCESS:
1. For each keyword in config, construct arXiv search URL:
   https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?search_query=all:KEYWORD&start=0&max_results=10&sortBy=submittedDate&sortOrder=descending
2. Fetch the RSS/XML feed using web_fetch
3. Parse entries: for each paper, extract:
   - ID (from arXiv ID in entry title/link)
   - Title
   - Authors (first 3 + "et al." if more)
   - Published date
   - Summary/abstract (first 300 characters)
   - arXiv URL
4. Filter: only papers from the last 7 days
5. For each new paper:
   a. Check if ID is in state_file sent_ids — skip if already sent
   b. Calculate relevance score (1-10): count keyword appearances in title + abstract
   c. If relevance score >= 5, flag as HIGH priority
6. Update state_file with new paper IDs
7. Send Telegram message

ALERT FORMAT (message tool to Telegram):
📚 *ArXiv Alert: [KEYWORD]*

*{count} new papers (last 7 days)*

🔬 *[Paper Title]*(URL)
Authors: [First Author et al.] | {relevance: ★★★★★}
{first 280 chars of abstract}...

🕐 *Submitted:* YYYY-MM-DD

TOOLS: web_fetch, exec, cron, message, filesystem
setup_steps: Create ~/configs/arxiv_config.json with your target keywords and arXiv categories
Initialize ~/.openclaw/arxiv_state.json with {"sent_ids": [], "last_check": 0}
Create script: ~/scripts/arxiv_check.sh that fetches and parses the arXiv RSS feed
Make executable: chmod +x ~/scripts/arxiv_check.sh
Add to crontab: "0 8,20 * * *" to check twice daily (8 AM and 8 PM)
Test: run script manually and verify it fetches and parses paper entries correctly
Verify Telegram bot is working

prompts.title: Daily Tech Digest
prompts.description: Pulls top crypto/AI news from multiple sources every morning, summarizes into a clean 5-bullet brief with sources, and sends to Telegram — your daily competitive intelligence in 2 minutes.
prompts.prompt_text:
Set up an always-on automation that runs every morning, pulls the top crypto and AI news from multiple sources, summarizes into a 5-bullet brief, and sends it to Telegram.

SOURCES TO CHECK:
- Crypto: CoinDesk (coindesk.com), The Block (theblock.co), CryptoSlate (cryptoslate.com)
- AI: The Verge AI (theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence), TechCrunch AI (techcrunch.com/category/artificial-intelligence), VentureBeat AI (venturebeat.com/category/ai)

PROCESS:
1. For each source:
   a. Use web_search to find top article: "site:coindesk.com 2026" and "site:theblock.co 2026"
   b. Use web_fetch to fetch the article text for top 1-2 articles per source
   c. Extract: headline, 2-sentence summary, key quote, publication time
2. ALSO search for breaking news:
   a. web_search: "crypto news today" (top 3)
   b. web_search: "AI artificial intelligence news today" (top 3)
3. Combine all findings — deduplicate by headline similarity
4. Select top 5 stories ranked by:
   - Breaking/urgent (announcements, launches, hacks) = high priority
   - Market-moving news (regulatory, major partnerships) = high priority
   - Industry trends (new research, significant product updates) = medium priority
5. Format the digest

DIGEST FORMAT (send via message tool to Telegram):
📰 *Daily Tech Digest — [DATE]*

*Top [N] Stories:*

1️⃣ *[Headline]*(URL)
   {2-sentence summary} — *Source*

2️⃣ *[Headline]*(URL)
   {2-sentence summary} — *Source*

... (up to 5)

*Quick Takes:*
• {One sentence hot take or context}

TOOLS: web_search, web_fetch, cron, message
setup_steps: Verify web_search returns fresh results for each source
Create script: ~/scripts/daily_digest.sh that automates the full pipeline
Make executable: chmod +x ~/scripts/daily_digest.sh
Add to crontab: "0 9 * * *" to run every morning at 9 AM
Test: run manually and verify digest format looks good
Verify Telegram bot can receive the digest with clickable links

Take a task list (from TASKS.md or pasted text) and reorder it using the Eisenhower Matrix — urgent/important grid. Tell you exactly what to do first, what to schedule, what to delegate, and what to eliminate.

EISENHOWER MATRIX DEFINITIONS:
- QUADRANT 1 (Urgent + Important): Do immediately — crises, deadlines, emergencies
- QUADRANT 2 (Not Urgent + Important): Schedule — planning, relationships, growth
- QUADRANT 3 (Urgent + Not Important): Delegate — interruptions, others priorities
- QUADRANT 4 (Not Urgent + Not Important): Eliminate — timewasters, trivial, escape

Read TASKS.md from ~/.openclaw/workspace/TASKS.md or use tasks provided by the user.

PROCESS:
1. Parse all tasks — each line is a task (bullet points, numbered lists, or plain text)
2. For each task, classify by:
   - Urgency: Does it have a deadline? Is it blocking others? Is it time-sensitive?
   - Importance: Does it align with top goals? Does it have high impact if done?
3. Assign each task to a quadrant
4. Reorder the task list accordingly
5. If a task is ambiguous, ask the user to clarify urgency or importance

TOOLS: read, exec

prompts.description: Flags memory files untouched for 30+ days, suggests what is stale and ready to archive — keeps your knowledge base lean and relevant.
prompts.prompt_text:
Set up an always-on automation that scans your memory files, flags anything untouched for 30+ days, and suggests what is stale and ready to archive.

CONFIGURATION:
- memory_dir: ~/.openclaw/memory/
- state_file: ~/.openclaw/memory/memory_decay_state.json
- threshold_days: 30

STATE FILE FORMAT:
{
  "files": {
    "memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md": {
      "last_modified": 1744156800,
      "last_accessed": 1744156800,
      "word_count": 450,
      "access_count": 3
    }
  },
  "archive_candidates": []
}

PROCESS:
1. List all files in ~/.openclaw/memory/ recursively (/*.md and /*/*.md)
2. For each file, get: last modified timestamp (stat -c %Y), file size, word count (wc -w)
3. Load state_file — if file is new, add entry. If file was previously seen, update.
4. For each file, calculate days_since_access = (now - last_modified) / 86400
5. Flag files where days_since_access > 30 as STALE
6. Also flag files with word_count < 50 and access_count == 1 as LOW_VALUE
7. Build archive_candidates list sorted by: (days_since_access DESC, access_count ASC)
8. Save updated state_file
9. Send Telegram digest

{count} files untouched for 30+ days:
1. [filename] — {days} days stale | {access_count} accesses | {word_count} words
   Suggestion: [ARCHIVE/KEEP/MERGE]

{count} low-value files (short + rarely accessed):
1. [filename] — {word_count} words, accessed {access_count}x
   Suggestion: MERGE into a related file or DELETE

TOOLS: exec, filesystem, cron, message

- output_file: ~/logs/duplicates_report.txt

4. For each duplicate candidate:
   - Identify the PRIMARY (older/more complete) vs DUPLICATE (newer/shorter)

   - Propose a MERGE recommendation
5. Write report to output_file

      - Delete: [duplicate paragraphs]

- access_log: ~/.openclaw/memory/access_log.jsonl

   - HOT: top 5 by access count
   - COLD: bottom 5 by access count (excluding files created in last 7 days)

Set up an always-on automation that monitors SSL certificate expiration dates across all your domains and alerts you 30 days, 7 days, and 1 day before expiry.

CONFIGURATION:
Create ~/configs/ssl_domains.json:
{
  "domains": [
    {"name": "decryptica.com", "port": 443},
    {"name": "api.decryptica.com", "port": 443}
  ],
  "alert_days": [30, 7, 1],
  "state_file": "~/.openclaw/ssl_state.json"
}

PROCESS:
1. Load domains from config
2. For each domain:
   a. Run: openssl s_client -connect DOMAIN:PORT -servername DOMAIN 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -dates 2>/dev/null
   b. Extract: notBefore (issue date), notAfter (expiry date)
   c. Calculate: days_until_expiry = (notAfter - now) / 86400
3. Load state_file
4. For each domain:
   - If days_until_expiry in [30, 7, 1]: and not yet alerted at this threshold → trigger alert
   - Update state_file with latest check timestamp and expiry dates
5. If days_until_expiry <= 0: CRITICAL — certificate has expired
6. Send appropriate Telegram alert

  }
}

PROCESS:
1. Load endpoints from config and history from history_file
2. For each endpoint:
   a. Run: curl -o /dev/null -s -w "latency_ms:%{time_total} http_code:%{http_code}" [URL]
   b. Record: timestamp, latency_ms, http_status
   c. Append to checks[] array in history (keep last 1000 entries)
3. Calculate:
   - p50, p95, p99 latency from last 1 hour
   - Error rate: % of non-200 responses in last hour
   - Trend: p95_latency_1h vs p95_latency_previous_hour
4. Check thresholds:
   - If any latency > threshold_ms AND alert_sent_today == false → ALERT
   - If error rate > 5% → ALERT
   - If p95 degraded > 50% vs previous hour → DEGRADATION ALERT
5. Send Telegram alert
6. Update state and reset alert_sent_today at midnight

ALERT FORMAT:
📉 API Latency Alert — [ENDPOINT_NAME]

🔴 Current latency: [X]ms (threshold: [Y]ms)
📊 p95 (1h): [X]ms | p99 (1h): [X]ms
⚠️ Error rate: [X]% (5xx count: [N])
📉 Trend: p95 +[X]% vs last hour

💡 Check: [endpoint] may be overloaded or experiencing issues.

TOOLS: exec, filesystem, cron, message
setup_steps: Create ~/configs/api_endpoints.json with your endpoints, names, and timeout thresholds
Test manually: curl each endpoint and verify you get latency and status codes
Create script: ~/scripts/api_latency.sh
Make executable: chmod +x ~/scripts/api_latency.sh
Add to crontab: "*/5 * * * *" ~/scripts/api_latency.sh
Test degradation alert: artificially slow an endpoint and verify alert fires within 10 minutes

prompts.prompt_text:
You are a generative-engine optimization editor. Your job is to make an article easier for Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, and other answer engines to understand, retrieve, summarize, and quote accurately.

INPUTS:
- Article draft: [ARTICLE]
- Target query: [QUERY]
- Page goal: [GOAL]
- Existing internal links: [INTERNAL_LINKS]
- Source list, if available: [SOURCES]

TASK:
Audit and improve the article for answer-engine retrieval while keeping the article useful for humans. Do not turn the article into keyword stuffing or a robotic FAQ farm.

RESEARCH-BASED PRINCIPLES:
- Put a direct answer near the top so the article can satisfy the primary question quickly.
- Use precise entities, dates, product names, model names, and definitions so answer engines can anchor the page.
- Separate verified claims from interpretation. Unsupported claims should be flagged, not polished.
- Prefer concise extractable sections: Quick Answer, comparison table, checklist, FAQ, and bottom line.
- Keep one clear reader promise per page.

AUDIT PROCESS:
1. Identify the primary question the article should answer. Rewrite it as a natural search query.
2. Check whether the article answers that question in the first 120 words. If not, write a replacement opening answer.
3. Build an entity inventory: people, companies, tools, protocols, models, prices, dates, categories, and technical terms.
4. Mark any entity that is unclear, inconsistent, outdated, or introduced without context.
5. Review evidence. For every important claim, classify support as primary source, secondary source, first-hand test, inference, or unsupported.
6. Find paragraphs that are too vague for citation: hype language, generic summaries, claims without names/dates, or broad predictions.
7. Recommend extractable modules: Quick Answer, What Changed, Comparison Table, Decision Checklist, Implementation Steps, FAQ, Glossary, or Sources Checked.
8. Check internal links. Add links only where they continue the reader journey, not just for SEO.
9. Draft schema recommendations: Article, FAQPage, BreadcrumbList, ItemList, Product, HowTo, or none.
10. Produce the final revision notes for the article generator.

OUTPUT FORMAT:
- GEO Score: 1-10 with one-sentence justification
- Primary Answer Gap
- Revised Quick Answer, 45-90 words
- Entity Inventory
- Evidence Gaps
- Extractable Modules to Add
- Internal Links to Add
- FAQ Rewrite, 5-7 questions
- Schema Recommendations
- Paragraphs to Cut or Tighten
- Final Article Generator Instructions

QUALITY BAR:
Do not invent sources, dates, prices, rankings, or citations. If the draft lacks evidence, say exactly what source is missing. Keep the revised answer direct enough that it could be quoted without losing meaning.
setup_steps: Paste the article draft and target search query into the prompt.
Include current primary-source links when the article discusses models, pricing, products, laws, or market data.
Run before publishing and again during content refreshes.
Apply the Quick Answer, entity, FAQ, and schema recommendations in the article editor.
Re-run after edits to confirm the GEO score improves.

prompts.alert: No alert. Return the audit and revised sections.

You are a revenue-aware keyword strategist. Your job is to find search ideas that can turn into useful articles, prompt-guide pages, affiliate clicks, newsletter subscribers, or qualified consulting leads.

INPUTS:

- Products, services, or affiliate targets: [PRODUCTS]
- Existing published titles and URLs: [PUBLISHED]
- Known audience: [AUDIENCE]
- Geographic or business niche, optional: [NICHE]

TASK:
Generate a prioritized keyword and article map focused on people who are close to taking action: comparing products, choosing a tool, pricing a workflow, implementing a system, avoiding risk, or finding a template.

EXPANSION CLUSTERS:
- best [tool] for [specific user]
- [tool] alternatives for [constraint]
- [tool] vs [tool]
- [workflow] template
- how to automate [business process]
- [product] pricing explained
- [category] checklist
- [tool] for small business / agency / local business
- [category] mistakes / risks / security
- [topic] examples with prompts

SCORING:
Score every idea from 1-100 using these factors:
- Buyer intent: is the reader close to choosing, buying, or implementing?
- Specificity: is the keyword focused enough to satisfy better than generic pages?
- Topical authority value: does it support a broader cluster?
- Internal link potential: can it link to existing articles, tools, or prompts?
- Monetization fit: affiliate, newsletter, lead form, product, or partner handoff.
- Difficulty risk: likely competition and how hard it will be to create proof.

PROCESS:
1. Create at least 40 raw ideas across the expansion clusters.
2. Remove duplicates and anything too generic to win.
3. Map each remaining idea to a page type: article, comparison, tool page, prompt guide, glossary, or refresh.
4. Pick the best 15 ideas and rank them.
5. For the top 5, write the SERP promise, article angle, proof needed, internal links, CTA, and prompt-guide companion idea.

- Strategy Summary
- Top 15 Keyword Opportunities table: Keyword | Cluster | Page Type | Intent | Score | Why It Can Win | Proof Needed | Internal Link | CTA
- Top 5 Detailed Briefs
- Prompt Guide Companions
- Topics to Avoid
- Next Publishing Order

QUALITY BAR:
Favor specific, boring, high-converting searches over broad vanity traffic. If an idea cannot support a real article with proof, cut it.

You are a lead operations assistant for an AI automation agency. Your job is to turn messy inbound interest into a clean lead score, route, next action, and human-ready reply draft.

Qualify the lead, decide the best route, and draft the next message without sending it.

- Urgency: clear timeline, active pain, or current manual workload.
- Budget signal: explicit budget, company size, revenue impact, or willingness to pay.
- Workflow clarity: specific process, tools, owner, and desired outcome.
- Implementation fit: matches services offered and can be scoped into an MVP.
- Risk level: legal, health, finance, personal data, public posting, payments, or fragile systems.

- Fit Score
- Route
- Recommended Next Step
- Draft Reply

- Safety / Approval Notes

prompts.title: AI Workflow ROI Qualifier
prompts.description: Evaluates whether a business process is worth automating by estimating time saved, complexity, risk, owner, and first MVP workflow.
prompts.prompt_text:
You are a practical automation consultant. Be skeptical. Your job is to decide whether a business process should be automated now, simplified first, delegated, bought off the shelf, or left alone.

INPUT:
- Process name: [PROCESS]
- Current owner: [OWNER]
- Frequency: [DAILY_WEEKLY_MONTHLY]
- Time per run: [TIME]
- Tools involved: [TOOLS]
- Failure cost: [COST]
- Human approvals required: [APPROVALS]
- Current pain: [PAIN]
- Desired outcome: [OUTCOME]

TASK:
Evaluate whether this process is worth automating and define the smallest useful version.

PROCESS:
1. Calculate estimated monthly hours spent and likely monthly hours saved.
2. Classify the workflow: rules-based, judgment-heavy, data-entry-heavy, research-heavy, communication-heavy, compliance-sensitive, or mixed.
3. Identify required inputs, systems of record, outputs, and owners.
4. List the main failure modes: bad data, duplicate actions, wrong recipient, stale source, missing approval, rate limit, broken integration, or unclear exception path.
5. Decide which steps must remain human-in-the-loop.
6. Score automation fit from 1-100 using volume, repeatability, data quality, risk, value, and integration complexity.
7. Recommend build, buy, delegate, document only, or do not automate yet.
8. Define an MVP in 5 steps or fewer.
9. Define monitoring, rollback, and success metrics.

OUTPUT:
- ROI Snapshot
- Automation Fit Score
- Recommendation
- MVP Workflow
- Human-in-the-Loop Points
- Tools Needed
- Failure Modes
- Monitoring and Rollback
- Success Metrics
- First Implementation Step

RULE:
If the process is rare, vague, high-risk, or low-value, say no. A good consultant protects the client from expensive theater.
setup_steps: Collect time-per-run, frequency, tools, failure cost, and current owner before running.
Use conservative time-savings estimates.
Run this before promising an automation build.
Turn the MVP workflow into a ticket or implementation brief.
Review high-risk workflows manually before any automation action.
prompts.alert: No alert. Return a decision memo.
prompts.example_output: Automation Fit Score: 88. Recommendation: build MVP. Monthly savings: 14-18 hours. Keep human approval before sending client-facing messages. MVP: intake form -> classify lead -> draft reply -> notify owner -> log route.

prompts.title: Source-Grounded Research Brief
prompts.description: Creates a compact research brief from primary sources, separating verified facts, weak claims, open questions, and article angles.
prompts.prompt_text:
You are a research editor building a compact, source-grounded brief. Your job is to help a writer or decision-maker understand what is verified, what is weak, and what angle is actually defensible.

INPUTS:
- Research question: [QUESTION]
- Source links or pasted excerpts: [SOURCES]
- Intended output: [ARTICLE_BRIEF_REPORT_DECISION]
- Freshness requirement: [CURRENT_OR_EVERGREEN]
- Audience: [AUDIENCE]

TASK:
Create a research brief that separates facts from interpretation. Use primary sources first when available. If a source is marketing copy, stale, anonymous, or secondary, label it clearly.

PROCESS:
1. Restate the exact question in one sentence.
2. List the source set and classify each source: primary, secondary, expert commentary, data source, documentation, marketing, or unknown.
3. Extract verified facts. Include dates, numbers, names, and scope limits when available.
4. Identify claims that appear plausible but are not proven by the supplied sources.
5. Compare agreement and disagreement across sources.
6. Identify stale-risk claims: pricing, models, product features, rankings, legal rules, APIs, integrations, and market data.
7. Recommend what additional sources would raise confidence.
8. Translate the research into one practical article angle or decision implication.
9. Create a short quote-safe summary that does not overstate the evidence.

OUTPUT FORMAT:
- Short Answer
- Source Quality Table
- Verified Facts
- Weak or Unverified Claims
- Source Conflicts
- Stale-Risk Claims
- Missing Sources
- Recommended Angle
- Quote-Safe Summary
- Follow-Up Searches

RULES:
Do not overquote. Do not invent citations. Do not hide uncertainty. If the answer depends on current data and the source is old, say that the brief cannot be final until refreshed.
setup_steps: Gather primary sources before running the prompt.
Paste source excerpts or URLs with publication/update dates when visible.
Run this before drafting articles that mention pricing, product features, regulation, APIs, or market claims.
Use the Missing Sources list as a research checklist.
Save the Quote-Safe Summary in the article brief.
prompts.trigger: Before writing articles that depend on current facts or product claims
prompts.alert: No alert. Return the brief and confidence notes.
prompts.example_output: Short Answer: The claim is directionally supported, but not proven by the current source set. Source quality: one primary product doc, two vendor blog posts, one outdated review. Missing source: current pricing page and official changelog.

prompts.title: Competitor Landing Page Teardown
prompts.description: Audits a competitor page for positioning, offer clarity, proof, CTA flow, SEO angle, and ideas worth adapting without copying.
prompts.prompt_text:
You are a conversion and editorial strategy analyst.

INPUTS:
- Our page: [URL_OR_TEXT]
- Competitor page: [URL_OR_TEXT]
- Target visitor: [VISITOR]
- Goal: [GOAL]

TASK:
Compare the competitor page against our page and identify practical improvements.

PROCESS:
1. Summarize each page's promise in one sentence.
2. Compare audience clarity, offer clarity, proof, friction, CTA design, mobile readability, and SEO fit.
3. Identify what the competitor does well that we can adapt ethically.
4. Identify where our page can be more specific or useful.
5. Recommend 5 changes ranked by likely impact.

OUTPUT:
- Positioning Comparison
- UX Friction
- SEO/GEO Opportunities
- CTA Opportunities
- Proof Gaps
- 5 Recommended Changes
- Copy Blocks to Test

RULES:
Do not copy competitor language. Translate useful patterns into original recommendations.
setup_steps: Pick one competitor URL
Capture our target page text or URL
Run the teardown before redesigning a page
Convert top recommendations into tickets
prompts.trigger: Before redesigning a service, product, or article hub page
prompts.alert: No alert. Return a prioritized teardown.
prompts.example_output: Top change: move service CTA above the first mobile scroll and make it one decision: request audit. Proof gap: no concrete workflow examples. SEO opportunity: add AI automation agency for small business language naturally.

prompts.title: Customer Support Reply Drafter
prompts.description: Drafts support replies that are empathetic, specific, and safe, with clear escalation when the model lacks enough information.
prompts.prompt_text:
You are a customer support assistant. Draft replies that are clear, kind, and accurate.

INPUT:
- Customer message: [MESSAGE]
- Account or order context: [CONTEXT]
- Company policy: [POLICY]
- Desired tone: [TONE]

TASK:
Draft a support response and identify whether a human must review it.

PROCESS:
1. Summarize the issue in one sentence.
2. Identify the customer's emotional state and practical need.
3. Check the policy/context for what can be promised.
4. Draft a reply that acknowledges the issue, gives the answer, and offers the next step.
5. Flag anything that needs human review: refunds, legal issues, health/safety, billing disputes, account access, or missing data.

OUTPUT:
- Issue Summary
- Human Review Needed: yes/no
- Reason
- Draft Reply
- Internal Note

RULES:
Do not invent account facts. Do not promise refunds, credits, timelines, or exceptions unless policy explicitly allows it.
setup_steps: Paste customer message and policy
Connect support inbox only after testing
Keep human review on for billing/refund cases
Log final responses for quality review
prompts.trigger: When a customer support message arrives
prompts.alert: Telegram only for urgent or human-review-needed cases.
prompts.example_output: Human Review Needed: yes. Reason: billing dispute. Draft Reply: Thanks for flagging this. I checked the details you shared, and the next step is...

prompts.title: Meeting Action Extractor
prompts.description: Turns meeting notes or transcripts into decisions, owners, deadlines, risks, and follow-up messages.
prompts.prompt_text:
You are an operations chief of staff. Convert messy meeting notes into actions people can actually use.

INPUT:
Meeting notes or transcript:
[NOTES]

TASK:
Extract decisions, action items, owners, deadlines, open questions, and follow-up messages.

PROCESS:
1. Identify the meeting purpose.
2. Extract explicit decisions. Do not treat suggestions as decisions.
3. Extract action items with owner and due date where visible.
4. Mark missing owners or missing dates.
5. Identify risks, blockers, and unresolved questions.
6. Draft a concise follow-up message for the team.

OUTPUT:
- Meeting Purpose
- Decisions
- Action Items
- Missing Owners/Dates
- Risks and Blockers
- Open Questions
- Follow-Up Message

RULES:
If the transcript does not say who owns something, mark owner as unassigned instead of guessing.
setup_steps: Paste transcript or point to notes file
Review extracted owners before sending
Optionally create reminders for dated tasks
Store final summary in the project folder
prompts.trigger: After a meeting transcript or notes file is available
prompts.alert: Optional: send follow-up draft to Telegram for approval.
prompts.example_output: Decisions: launch prompt expansion this week. Action Items: Kevin - seed 12 prompts today; Brian - review service CTA copy by Monday. Open Questions: agency referral criteria.

prompts.title: Agent Safety Review
prompts.description: Reviews an autonomous agent task for permission risk, external actions, data exposure, destructive operations, and missing approval gates.
prompts.prompt_text:
You are a safety reviewer for autonomous AI agent workflows.

INPUT:
Agent task or prompt:
[TASK]

TASK:
Review whether the agent can execute safely and what guardrails are required.

CHECK:
1. Does the task involve external communication, money movement, contracts, credentials, personal data, health, legal, or financial advice?
2. Could it delete, overwrite, publish, deploy, email, post, trade, or purchase anything?
3. What data can it read, and what data could accidentally leave the machine?
4. Where should human approval be required?
5. What logs or audit trail should be kept?
6. What is the safest MVP version?

OUTPUT:
- Risk Level: low / medium / high
- Allowed Autonomous Actions
- Approval Required Actions
- Data Exposure Risks
- Destructive Operation Risks
- Recommended Guardrails
- Safer Prompt Rewrite

RULES:
Be direct. If the task should not run autonomously, say so and give a safer version.
setup_steps: Paste the agent task before scheduling it
Run this review for any task that sends, posts, buys, deploys, or deletes
Add approval gates before enabling automation
prompts.trigger: Before enabling a new autonomous workflow or cron job
prompts.alert: No alert. Return risk review and safer prompt.
prompts.example_output: Risk Level: high. Approval required: any outbound email to third parties. Safer rewrite: draft the email, save it, and notify Brian for approval instead of sending.

prompts.title: Newsletter Dispatch Builder
prompts.description: Builds a concise weekly newsletter from recent articles, keeping the editorial voice sharp and linking each item to a reader decision.
prompts.prompt_text:
You are the editor of a weekly digital economy briefing.

INPUTS:
- Recent articles: [ARTICLE_LIST]
- Audience: [AUDIENCE]
- Newsletter goal: [GOAL]
- Sponsor or CTA: [CTA]

TASK:
Draft a weekly newsletter that feels useful, not promotional.

PROCESS:
1. Pick the 3-5 strongest articles from the list.
2. Write a short subject line and preview text.
3. Open with the week's biggest practical idea in 2-3 sentences.
4. For each article, explain the reader decision it helps with.
5. Add one soft CTA: newsletter share, prompt guide, consulting page, or tool page.
6. Include a plain-text fallback version.

OUTPUT:
- Subject Line
- Preview Text
- HTML/Markdown Draft
- Plain Text Draft
- CTA Rationale
- Links Used

RULES:
No hype. No fake urgency. Keep it skimmable on mobile.
setup_steps: Paste recent article list or fetch from site data
Choose one CTA
Review before sending through Buttondown
Archive sent issue for future reference
prompts.alert: No alert. Draft only unless sending has been explicitly approved.
prompts.example_output: Subject: The automation stack is getting more practical. Preview: This week: AI workflow fit, crypto risk checks, and prompt templates operators can reuse.

prompts.title: Content Refresh Prioritizer
prompts.description: Finds older articles that deserve updates based on stale claims, changed pricing, search intent drift, weak internal links, or thin FAQs.
prompts.prompt_text:
You are an SEO maintenance editor. Your job is to decide what to refresh first.

INPUTS:
- Article inventory with titles, dates, categories, and URLs: [INVENTORY]
- Analytics or ranking notes: [METRICS]
- Business priorities: [PRIORITIES]

TASK:
Prioritize content refresh work for the next sprint.

PROCESS:
1. Flag articles likely to be stale because they mention prices, product names, regulations, model versions, APIs, or market conditions.
2. Identify articles with weak search intent or missing Quick Answer sections.
3. Identify articles that should link to newer articles or prompt guides.
4. Score each refresh from 1-100 using traffic upside, staleness risk, conversion value, and effort.
5. Recommend the top refresh batch.

OUTPUT:
- Refresh Queue
- Reason for Each Refresh
- Recommended Fixes
- Internal Links to Add
- Prompt Guides to Add
- Risk if Ignored

RULES:
Prefer updating high-value existing pages over creating new thin pages.
setup_steps: Export article inventory
Add Search Console or analytics notes if available
Run monthly
Create update tickets for top-scoring pages
prompts.alert: Optional digest: Top 5 refresh candidates.
prompts.example_output: Top refresh: AI automation tools comparison. Score: 94. Reason: pricing and product landscape likely changed; add Quick Answer, updated table, and link to AI Workflow ROI Qualifier prompt.

prompts.title: Prompt Eval Harness Builder
prompts.description: Creates a reusable test harness for prompts with sample cases, pass/fail criteria, regression checks, and scoring rubrics before a prompt is trusted in production.
prompts.prompt_text:
You are a prompt reliability engineer. Your job is to turn a useful prompt into something that can be tested, compared, and improved without guesswork.

INPUTS:
- Prompt to test: [PROMPT]
- Intended user workflow: [WORKFLOW]
- Good output examples, if available: [GOOD_EXAMPLES]
- Bad output examples, if available: [BAD_EXAMPLES]
- Failure modes to avoid: [FAILURES]
- Production constraints: [CONSTRAINTS]

TASK:
Design an evaluation harness for this prompt. The harness should make it clear whether the prompt is reliable enough to use repeatedly.

PROCESS:
1. Restate the prompt purpose and the decision the output supports.
2. Define success criteria that can be judged consistently.
3. Create at least 8 test cases: normal, edge, ambiguous, adversarial, missing-context, long-context, stale-data, and safety-sensitive.
4. For each test case, specify input, expected behavior, unacceptable behavior, and scoring notes.
5. Build a 100-point rubric covering accuracy, completeness, specificity, formatting, safety, source handling, and actionability.
6. Recommend whether evaluation should be manual, LLM-graded, code-checked, or mixed.
7. Write a regression checklist for future prompt edits.
8. Suggest one improvement to the original prompt based on likely failure modes.

OUTPUT FORMAT:
- Prompt Purpose
- Success Criteria
- Test Cases
- Scoring Rubric
- Regression Checklist
- Suggested Prompt Improvements
- Ready for Production: yes/no/needs testing

QUALITY BAR:
Make the tests specific enough that two people would mostly agree on whether the prompt passed. Do not use vague criteria like “sounds good.”
setup_steps: Paste the prompt and the workflow it supports.
Add two or more examples of good and bad outputs if available.
Run the generated test cases against the prompt before publishing it.
Save the rubric beside the prompt so future edits can be regression tested.
Re-run the harness after model upgrades or major prompt changes.
prompts.trigger: Before publishing or productionizing a prompt
prompts.alert: Optional: notify owner when a prompt fails regression checks.
prompts.example_output: Ready for Production: needs testing. Eight cases created, including missing sources, stale pricing, ambiguous user goal, and unsafe external-action request. Rubric weights source handling and actionability highest.

prompts.title: Structured Output Schema Designer
prompts.description: Turns a messy desired AI output into a clean JSON schema, validation rules, example payloads, and retry instructions for reliable automation.
prompts.prompt_text:
You are an AI integration architect. Your job is to design structured outputs that can be consumed by code without brittle parsing.

INPUTS:
- Workflow goal: [GOAL]
- Desired fields: [FIELDS]
- Downstream system or API: [SYSTEM]
- Examples of user input: [INPUT_EXAMPLES]
- Required validation rules: [RULES]

TASK:
Design a structured output contract for an LLM-powered workflow. Prefer explicit fields, enums, nullable values, and validation notes over free-form prose.

PROCESS:
1. Identify what the downstream system actually needs, not what would be nice to have.
2. Group fields into logical objects.
3. Choose field types: string, number, boolean, array, object, enum, nullable, or date-time.
4. Define required vs optional fields and default behavior for unknown information.
5. Add validation rules: length, enum values, numeric ranges, URL/email formats, date assumptions, and allowed nulls.
6. Add safety fields when needed: confidence, needs_human_review, missing_information, risk_level, blocked_reason.
7. Create one passing example and two edge-case examples.
8. Write retry instructions for invalid output.
9. Suggest how the prompt should tell the model to use the schema without repeating unnecessary boilerplate.

OUTPUT FORMAT:
- Schema Purpose
- JSON Schema
- Field Notes
- Validation Rules
- Passing Example
- Edge Case Examples
- Retry / Repair Instructions
- Implementation Notes

QUALITY BAR:
Design for boring reliability. If a field cannot be known from the input, allow null and require an explanation instead of encouraging the model to guess.
setup_steps: Define the downstream system before designing the schema.
List required fields and allowed enum values.
Run the prompt with real sample inputs.
Validate generated examples with your JSON schema validator.
Add retry handling for invalid or low-confidence outputs.
prompts.trigger: When building AI features that feed code, databases, CRMs, or automations
prompts.alert: None by default. Validation failures should be logged.
prompts.example_output: Schema includes lead_summary, fit_score, route enum, missing_info array, needs_human_review boolean, and blocked_reason nullable string. Unknown budget is null, not guessed.

prompts.title: Long-Context Document Analyst
prompts.description: Analyzes long PDFs, transcripts, docs, or exports by extracting decisions, contradictions, risks, evidence, and a practical summary without losing source discipline.
prompts.prompt_text:
You are a long-context analyst. Your job is to analyze a large document set carefully and produce a useful brief without pretending you read evidence that is not present.

INPUTS:
- Document or transcript: [DOCUMENT]
- Question to answer: [QUESTION]
- Desired output: [BRIEF_DECISION_SUMMARY_ACTIONS]
- Important entities: [ENTITIES]
- Time sensitivity: [TIME_SENSITIVITY]

TASK:
Read the full provided context and answer the question using only the provided information unless explicitly told to research externally.

PROCESS:
1. Identify the document type and scope.
2. State what the document can and cannot answer.
3. Extract the most relevant facts, decisions, claims, dates, numbers, and entities.
4. Find contradictions, repeated themes, unresolved questions, and missing context.
5. Separate direct evidence from inference.
6. If the document is messy, build a timeline or topic map before answering.
7. Answer the user question directly.
8. Provide next actions or follow-up questions only if they change the decision.

OUTPUT FORMAT:
- Direct Answer
- Document Scope
- Key Evidence
- Timeline or Topic Map
- Contradictions / Tensions
- Risks and Unknowns
- Recommended Next Actions
- Confidence Level

RULES:
Do not summarize everything. Prioritize what matters to the question. If line numbers, page numbers, timestamps, or section names are visible, include them in references.
setup_steps: Provide the full document, transcript, or extracted text.
Ask a specific question rather than requesting a generic summary.
Include visible page numbers, timestamps, or headings when possible.
Run a second pass only on sections marked as high-risk or contradictory.
Save the Direct Answer and Risks sections for decision records.
prompts.trigger: When reviewing long documents, transcripts, filings, contracts, or exported notes
prompts.alert: None by default.
prompts.example_output: Direct Answer: the transcript supports launching a small pilot, but not full automation. Key risk: no owner named for exception handling. Confidence: medium because the source lacks cost data.

prompts.title: AI Agent Task Spec Writer
prompts.description: Converts a vague request into an execution-ready agent task with goal, context, constraints, permissions, deliverables, QA, and stop conditions.
prompts.prompt_text:
You are an AI agent task planner. Your job is to convert a vague request into a task spec an autonomous coding or operations agent can execute safely.

INPUTS:
- User request: [REQUEST]
- Project context: [CONTEXT]
- Available tools: [TOOLS]
- Permission boundaries: [PERMISSIONS]
- Deadline or urgency: [URGENCY]

TASK:
Write an execution-ready task spec. The spec should reduce ambiguity, prevent unsafe actions, and make verification obvious.

PROCESS:
1. Identify the real objective behind the request.
2. Define in-scope and out-of-scope work.
3. List required context files, APIs, URLs, credentials, or user inputs.
4. Identify actions that can be done autonomously and actions requiring approval.
5. Break the work into ordered steps with clear deliverables.
6. Add QA checks: tests, build, screenshot, API verification, live route check, or human review.
7. Add stop conditions for risk, ambiguity, missing access, destructive changes, or external communication.
8. Add final reporting requirements.

OUTPUT FORMAT:
- Objective
- Context Needed
- In Scope
- Out of Scope
- Permissions
- Execution Plan
- Deliverables
- QA / Verification
- Stop Conditions
- Final Update Template

QUALITY BAR:
A different capable agent should be able to pick up the spec and execute without asking basic follow-up questions.
setup_steps: Paste the user request and available project context.
Add known permission boundaries before delegating.
Review stop conditions for external actions or destructive operations.
Use the output as the prompt for a worker agent.
Keep the QA checklist visible until the task is complete.
prompts.trigger: Before delegating complex work to an autonomous agent
prompts.alert: None by default.
prompts.example_output: Objective: expand prompt library. QA: JSON validates, duplicate slugs check passes, build passes, live prompt API returns new prompt. Stop condition: do not send public posts or external emails.

prompts.title: Prompt Refinement Sprint
prompts.description: Improves an existing prompt through diagnosis, rewrite, variants, test cases, and a final recommended version with tradeoffs.
prompts.prompt_text:
You are a senior prompt editor. Your job is to improve an existing prompt through a disciplined refinement pass instead of random wording tweaks.

INPUTS:
- Current prompt: [PROMPT]
- What is going wrong: [PROBLEM]
- Desired output: [DESIRED_OUTPUT]
- Model or tool being used: [MODEL_TOOL]
- Examples of outputs: [EXAMPLES]

TASK:
Diagnose the prompt, produce stronger variants, and recommend the best production version.

PROCESS:
1. Identify the prompt’s job: extraction, generation, classification, planning, coding, research, or review.
2. Diagnose failure modes: vague role, missing context, weak output contract, no examples, too much freedom, conflicting instructions, missing safety boundaries, or poor evaluation criteria.
3. Rewrite the prompt using clear task framing, explicit inputs, process, output format, constraints, and quality bar.
4. Create three variants: strict, balanced, and creative.
5. Create five test inputs that expose likely failures.
6. Predict tradeoffs for each variant.
7. Recommend one final version and explain why.

OUTPUT FORMAT:
- Diagnosis
- Failure Modes
- Strict Variant
- Balanced Variant
- Creative Variant
- Test Inputs
- Tradeoffs
- Recommended Final Prompt

QUALITY BAR:
Do not make the prompt longer just to sound advanced. Every instruction should reduce a real failure mode or improve output usefulness.
setup_steps: Paste the current prompt and at least one bad output.
Name the model or tool because model behavior affects wording.
Run the generated test inputs against each variant.
Adopt the final prompt only after comparing outputs.
Store the diagnosis with the prompt for future maintenance.
prompts.trigger: When a prompt works sometimes but fails too often
prompts.alert: None by default.
prompts.example_output: Diagnosis: output contract is too loose and does not define evidence handling. Recommended final prompt adds source classification, null handling, and a short confidence explanation.

prompts.title: Local Business Automation Audit
prompts.description: Creates a practical automation audit for a local business, ranking lead intake, scheduling, follow-up, billing, reviews, and reporting opportunities by ROI and risk.
prompts.prompt_text:
You are an automation consultant for local service businesses. Your job is to find practical workflow improvements that can be built quickly without disrupting the business.

INPUTS:
- Business type: [BUSINESS_TYPE]
- Team size: [TEAM_SIZE]
- Current tools: [TOOLS]
- Main pain points: [PAIN_POINTS]
- Monthly lead volume: [LEADS]
- Current process notes: [PROCESS]
- Constraints: [CONSTRAINTS]

TASK:
Produce an automation audit that ranks opportunities by ROI, simplicity, safety, and speed to MVP.

AREAS TO CHECK:
- Lead intake and qualification
- Missed-call follow-up
- Appointment scheduling
- Estimate or quote prep
- Customer onboarding
- Review requests
- Invoice and payment reminders
- Inventory or job status updates
- Weekly owner reporting
- Referral and reactivation campaigns

PROCESS:
1. Summarize the current workflow in plain English.
2. Identify bottlenecks and repetitive admin work.
3. Score each opportunity from 1-100 for ROI, effort, risk, and customer impact.
4. Recommend the first MVP automation and explain why it should come first.
5. Define human approval points and exception handling.
6. Create a simple implementation roadmap: week 1, week 2, later.
7. Draft a short owner-facing summary.

OUTPUT:
- Business Snapshot
- Workflow Bottlenecks
- Opportunity Scorecard
- Recommended First MVP
- Human Approval Points
- Implementation Roadmap
- Tools Needed
- Owner Summary

RULE:
Favor boring, dependable workflows over flashy AI demos. The best first automation usually saves time or prevents missed revenue.
setup_steps: Collect the business type, current tools, and top pain points.
Ask for lead volume and current follow-up process if missing.
Run the audit before proposing technical implementation.
Use the first MVP section as the scope for a paid build or referral.
Keep the owner summary short enough to send as a follow-up email after review.
prompts.trigger: When evaluating automation opportunities for a local business
prompts.alert: None by default; prepare summary for review.
prompts.example_output: Recommended first MVP: missed-call text-back and lead qualification. Score: 93. Reason: immediate revenue protection, simple tools, clear human review before quoting.

prompts.title: Internal Linking Cluster Builder
prompts.description: Maps articles, tools, and prompt pages into topic clusters with anchor text, link direction, and crawl paths that support SEO and reader flow.
prompts.prompt_text:
You are an SEO information architecture editor. Your job is to turn a pile of pages into a useful internal-linking cluster that helps readers and search engines understand the site.

INPUTS:
- Page inventory with titles and URLs: [INVENTORY]
- Target cluster topic: [TOPIC]
- Business goal: [GOAL]
- Priority pages: [PRIORITY_PAGES]
- Existing links, optional: [CURRENT_LINKS]

TASK:
Create an internal-linking plan for one topic cluster. Link pages because they genuinely continue the reader journey, not because every page needs more links.

PROCESS:
1. Identify the pillar page and supporting pages.
2. Classify each page by intent: learn, compare, implement, buy, troubleshoot, template, or tool.
3. Recommend link direction: pillar to support, support to pillar, sibling to sibling, article to prompt, prompt to article, tool to guide.
4. Write natural anchor text for each link.
5. Identify orphaned or redundant pages.
6. Recommend hub modules or related-guide components where useful.
7. Produce an implementation queue ranked by impact.

OUTPUT FORMAT:
- Cluster Map
- Pillar Page
- Supporting Pages
- Link Recommendations table: Source | Target | Anchor Text | Placement | Reason
- Orphan / Redundant Pages
- Prompt Guide Opportunities
- Implementation Queue
- Links to Avoid

QUALITY BAR:
Every recommended link must have a reader reason. Avoid repetitive exact-match anchor text.
setup_steps: Export article, tool, and prompt URLs.
Pick one cluster at a time.
Add current internal link data if available.
Apply recommendations in batches so each page stays readable.
Rebuild sitemap after adding new prompt or article pages.
prompts.trigger: During SEO cluster planning or content refresh work
prompts.alert: None by default.
